notes:
## Native plugins (C and C++ in games)
- A **plugin** asset brings C or C++ code into a game: its WebAssembly build runs in web builds, the Android web app and the Xbox Web player, and its native builds run in the C++ player on Windows, Linux, Android and the Xbox app. Games call it the same way everywhere: `const p = await IgnitePlugins.load('name'); p.call('fn', [numbers], [typedArrays])`.
- Plugins are saved in project folders as `Name.wasm` plus a file per native build, and Build for Xbox puts them in the package.
- A WebAssembly build missing an export the loader needs now gets an error that says which (for example, link with `--export-table`).

## Xbox
- **App or Game:** after Build and run on Xbox starts the game, Ignite3D reads from the console whether it runs as an App (about 1 GB and part of the GPU) or a Game (about 5 GB and the whole GPU), and says how to switch: Device Portal → Settings → Preference Settings → Treat UWP apps as games by default.
- New buttons in Build for Xbox: **Check app type**, **Show app log**, **Launch** (without rebuilding), **Uninstall from console**, and a list of consoles to switch between.
- The Xbox app writes `LocalState\app.log` (version, memory limit, App or Game, errors and crashes) and shows an error screen instead of a blank one. The Web player recovers when its browser engine stops or crashes. Games can read `IgniteHost.memoryLimit`.
- **Title-safe margin** (5% by default) keeps the game's UI inside the area TVs show; `Screen.safeArea` in C#, `get_display_safe_area()` in GDScript, and **Preview → Xbox** in the editor.
- Xbox services report that they're unavailable in the Windows & Xbox app instead of pretending to sign in (they need the Microsoft GDK), and the editor warns when a game uses them there.
- The Store guidance is corrected: the Xbox Store no longer takes new UWP games; games reach Xbox through ID@Xbox and the Microsoft GDK.
- Web games for Edge on Xbox: the "Press A" screen now starts sound and full screen reliably before handing the controller to the game, and updated builds don't mix old and new cached files.

## Smoother frames
- Physics is drawn smoothly between physics steps (Rigidbody interpolation), and frame times are smoothed so short hitches don't stutter.
- `Application.targetFrameRate` (C#) / `Time.targetFrameRate` now really limits the frame rate; the C++ player uses the display's vsync for it.

## Renderer fixes
- In the C++ players, materials' custom shader uniforms and vertex attributes now work (cartoon outlines and wind sway show up).
